title: Last Glacial Maximum lowstand state (eustatic, regional)

window.citation: Clark et al. 2009: ice sheets at LGM positions 26.5 ka to 19-20 ka

datum.citation: Lambeck et al. 2014: eustatic sea level fell slowly to -134 m between 29 and 21 ka, with a companion model peak fall of ~130 m; -120 m is the conservative round contour drawn here

frame: present-day WGS84, like the Cao et al. (2017) source polygons

method.description: boolean mask of ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second surface >= -120 m on the source grid, polygonised on cell boundaries as maximal rectangles, unioned, parts below 25 km2 dropped, simplified at 0.02 degrees with topology preserved, coordinates rounded to 4 decimals

evidence.editorial: EarthHistory modification after noaa-etopo-2022, lambeck-2014-sea-level, clark-lgm-2009, coles-1998-doggerland, gaffney-2009-doggerland, sturt-2013-inundation, bradley-2023-palaeo-sea-level, hall-2009-sundaland

limitations: eustatic only: a single flat -120 m datum, applied globally inside three footprints
no glacio-isostatic adjustment; relative sea level around an ice margin differed from the eustatic value by more than 100 m and varied over tens of kilometres
ice sheets are not drawn: ground under the Fennoscandian, British-Irish and Laurentide ice sheets is shown as exposed land, which it was not
ETOPO 2022 is modern bathymetry: sediment deposited, eroded and reworked since the LGM is not removed, and the present-day sea bed is not the lowstand land surface
regional: only the southern/central North Sea, the Sunda shelf and Beringia are drawn; every other coastline at this age falls back to the present-day composition
rivers, lakes, estuaries and the Doggerland landscape mapped by seismic survey are not represented at all

regional.statement: This is a regional state, not a global palaeogeography. Outside the three footprints the LGM interval draws no palaeo land and the present-day composition stays on screen.

beringia.title: Beringia and the Bering land bridge

source.license: NOAA / US Government work, public domain; attribution requested
source.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (2022). ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model. NOAA NCEI. https://doi.org/10.25921/fd45-gt74

doggerland-southern-north-sea.note: the southern North Sea plain between England, the Netherlands, north-west Germany and Denmark

sunda-shelf-core.note: the Sunda shelf between Sumatra, the Malay peninsula, Borneo and Java

bering-land-bridge.note: the eastern half of the Bering land bridge, Chukchi to Norton Sound

literatureComparison.note: Sturt et al. 2013 model 127,422 km2 of the North Sea zone submerged across the Holocene, a different quantity over a different window and under glacial isostatic adjustment; it is quoted as an order-of-magnitude anchor, not as agreement.

witnesses.note: Dogger Bank: subaerial at the lowstand, a shallow bank today
London: present-day land, unchanged by a sea-level lowstand
central Sunda shelf between Sumatra, Borneo and the Malay peninsula
Bering land bridge, north of St Lawrence Island
Norwegian Trench at -254 m: far below the lowstand datum, still sea
Makassar Strait: never closed by a lowstand (Hall 2009)
deep Aleutian Basin south of the shelf break: open ocean at the lowstand

references.citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information 2022. ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model. NOAA NCEI.
references.constrains: the present-day surface elevation and bathymetry the -120 m contour is taken from
references.claimOrInference: the elevations are the source's own measurement and model; reading them as a palaeo-shoreline is EarthHistory's inference

references.citation: Lambeck, K., Rouby, H., Purcell, A., Sun, Y. and Sambridge, M. 2014. Sea level and global ice volumes from the Last Glacial Maximum to the Holocene. PNAS 111, 15296-15303.
references.constrains: the eustatic datum: a slow fall to -134 m from 29 to 21 ka, with a companion model peak eustatic fall of ~130 m; -120 m is the conservative round figure this layer draws
references.claimOrInference: the eustatic values are claims of the source; the choice of -120 m and its application as a flat contour is EarthHistory's

references.citation: Clark, P. U., Dyke, A. S., Shakun, J. D., Carlson, A. E., Clark, J., Wohlfarth, B., Mitrovica, J. X., Hostetler, S. W. and McCabe, A. M. 2009. The Last Glacial Maximum. Science 325, 710-714.
references.constrains: the time window: 'Nearly all ice sheets were at their LGM positions from 26.5 ka to 19 to 20 ka'

references.citation: Coles, B. J. 1998. Doggerland: a speculative survey. Proceedings of the Prehistoric Society 64, 45-81.
references.constrains: that the exposed southern North Sea plain was a real, inhabited landscape, and that present-day North Sea relief 'does not provide a sound guide' to its former relief
references.claimOrInference: claim of the source; it is also the source's own warning against the method this layer uses

references.citation: Gaffney, V., Fitch, S. and Smith, D. 2009. Europe's Lost World: the Rediscovery of Doggerland. CBA Research Report 160, Council for British Archaeology, York.
references.constrains: the seismic mapping of the Doggerland landscape - rivers, lakes and coast - that this eustatic contour cannot reproduce

references.citation: Sturt, F., Garrow, D. and Bradley, S. 2013. New models of North West European Holocene palaeogeography and inundation. Journal of Archaeological Science 40, 3963-3976.
references.constrains: the GIA-modelled comparison figure: 127,422 km2 submerged in the North Sea zone, 'an area twice that of all the other three regions added together'
references.claimOrInference: model output of the source; quoted here only as the order-of-magnitude anchor for our own measured area

references.citation: Bradley, S. L., Ely, J. C., Clark, C. D., Edwards, R. J. and Shennan, I. 2023. Reconstruction of the palaeo-sea level of Britain and Ireland arising from empirical constraints of ice extent. Journal of Quaternary Science 38, 791-805.
references.constrains: why a flat eustatic contour is wrong in detail here: relative sea-level around Britain and Ireland varies by more than 100 m spatially under glacial isostatic adjustment
references.claimOrInference: the spatial variability is the source's claim; that it invalidates a flat contour in detail is EarthHistory's inference

references.citation: Hall, R. 2009. Southeast Asia's changing palaeogeography. Blumea 54, 148-161.
references.constrains: that a bathymetry-plus-eustasy reconstruction of the Sunda shelf is 'valid only for the Pleistocene', and that the Makassar Straits 'were never narrower than about 75 km'
